description: agent-hierarchy — SessionStart injects the resolved role→model table and the orchestration protocol on startup, resume, clear, fork, and post-compaction (so it survives compaction). It classifies the session three ways: a subagent (agent_id set) gets nothing, which is the intent here, since role agents carry their own instructions in agents/*.md and an Implementor that starts orchestrating would defeat the hierarchy; a top-level `claude --agent <hierarchy role>` session gets a short notice that it is NOT the Orchestrator; everything else gets the ordinary directive. The discriminator is agent_id, not agent_type — a top-level --agent session sets agent_type too, so testing it misclassifies a genuine main session as a subagent. Silent when the config sets enabled:false; with no config at all it emits a one-line nudge to run /hierarchy init. PreToolUse runs the ultra gate on Agent/Task/SendMessage: it holds Ultra-Advisor escalation for the user, whether dispatched as a subagent or via SendMessage to its named peer session — the first dispatch of each session is denied with instructions to put the decision to the user and record their answer (allow this session / ask each time / blocked this session) via hooks/gate.mjs; the answer is session-scoped and lives in ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.gate.json. Every other tool call, and every SendMessage not addressed to the Ultra-Advisor's peer, passes through untouched. SubagentStop runs the usage collector: it sums the finished subagent's transcript (token counts the harness already logged) into ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.usage.jsonl — plain node, zero model cost — which /hierarchy usage or hooks/usage-report.mjs renders as session/day/week/month reports. UserPromptSubmit also tracks the peer report-back contract: a delivered prompt carrying a `[hierarchy-peer-brief reply-to="..." task="..."]` sentinel inside its `<cross-session-message>` wrapper records a pending obligation in ~/.claude/agent-hierarchy.peer-pending.jsonl. PostToolUse (matcher SendMessage) resolves that obligation once a reply is sent to the recorded address, its name, or an explicit third-party reply-to. Stop blocks the session's turn from ending while an obligation is still owed, nudging at most twice before waiving it and allowing the stop regardless — fail-open throughout, and inert for subagents, exactly like the other hooks above. Enforcement arms only on a peer-delivered turn: UserPromptSubmit also arms a per-session turn marker whenever a wrapped message (a brief, a ping, or anything else carrying the cross-session-message envelope) leaves a pending obligation behind, and Stop's nudge/waive logic runs only on an armed turn, disarming it afterward either way — so a user directly chatting with a tasked peer neither triggers a nudge nor spends one.
